units.zh: 百官志一
units.en: Official Posts Treatise I
units.literal: Official Posts Treatise, Part One

units.zh: 官生於職，職沿於事，而名加之。
units.en: Offices grow out of duties, duties from tasks, and names are layered on top.
units.literal: Offices arise from duties; duties follow from affairs; and names are imposed upon them.

units.zh: 後世沿名，不究其實。
units.en: Later generations kept the titles without asking what they actually did.
units.literal: Later ages inherit the names without investigating the substance.

units.zh: 吏部，一太宰也，為大司徒，為尚書，為中書，為門下；
units.en: Personnel had been Grand Steward, then Grand Minister of Education, Secretariat Director, and Gate Chancellery;
units.literal: The Ministry of Personnel—once the Grand Steward—became Grand Minister of Education, became Director of the Department of State Affairs, became Secretariat Director, became Gate-of-the-Sons Chancellery;

units.zh: 兵部，一司馬也，為大司馬，為太尉，為樞密使。
units.en: War had been Minister of War, then Grand Minister of War, Grand Marshal, and Privy Commissioner.
units.literal: The Ministry of War—once the Minister of War—became Grand Minister of War, became Grand Marshal, became Privy Commissioner.

units.zh: 沿古官名，分今之職事以配之，於是先王統理天下之法，如治絲而棼，名實淆矣。
units.en: Later regimes kept ancient titles and mapped current duties onto them, so the old way of governing the realm became like untangling snarled silk—name and reality mixed together.
units.literal: Inheriting ancient office names, they matched present duties to them; thus the former kings' methods for ordering all under Heaven, like sorting silk that is already tangled, names and substance were confused.

units.zh: 契丹舊俗，事簡職專，官制樸實，不以名亂之，其興也勃焉。
units.en: In Khitan custom affairs were few and posts focused; government was plain and did not trade on empty titles, and their rise was swift.
units.literal: Khitan old custom: affairs were simple and duties exclusive; office institutions were plain and solid, not disturbed by names; their rise was swift indeed.

units.zh: 太祖神冊六年，詔正班爵。
units.en: In Taizu Shence year 6 ranks at court were fixed by edict.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Taizu's Shence reign an edict rectified court ranks.

units.zh: 至於太宗，兼制中國，官分南北，以國制治契丹，以漢制待漢人。
units.en: Under Taizong the state also ruled Chinese territory; offices split into Northern and Southern branches—Khitan governed by Liao law, Han by Han law.
units.literal: By Taizong's time he also administered China; offices were divided into Northern and Southern faces, governing Khitan by national institutions and treating Han by Han institutions.

units.zh: 國制簡樸，漢制則沿名之風固存也。
units.en: The native system stayed spare; within the Chinese system the habit of nominal inheritance persisted.
units.literal: National institutions were simple and plain; in Han institutions the habit of inheriting names still remained.

units.zh: 遼國官職，分北、南院，北面治宮帳、部族、屬國之政，南面治漢人州縣、租賦、軍馬之事。
units.en: Liao offices split into Northern and Southern Courts—the north handled palace accounts, tribes, and subject peoples; the south handled Han districts, revenue, and cavalry.
units.literal: Liao state offices were divided into Northern and Southern Courts: the Northern Face governed palace accounts, tribes, and subject states; the Southern Face governed Han prefectures and counties, taxes, and military horses.

units.zh: 因俗而治，得其宜矣。
units.en: Each branch ruled in its own way, which suited the realm.
units.literal: Governing according to custom, they obtained what was fitting.

units.zh: 初，太祖分叠剌夷離堇為北、南二大王，謂之北、南院。
units.en: Taizu first split the Dieci yilijin into Northern and Southern Great Kings—the Northern and Southern Courts.
units.literal: At first Taizu divided the Dieci yilijin into Northern and Southern Great Kings, called the Northern and Southern Courts.

units.zh: 宰相、樞密、宣徽、林牙，下至郎君、護衛，皆分北、南，其實所治皆北面之事，語遼官制者，可不辨。
units.en: Chancellor, Privy Council, xuanhui, linya, langjun, and guards all had north and south posts, but in practice they handled northern affairs; commentators on Liao offices should not be misled by the labels.
units.literal: Chancellors, Privy Council, Xuanhui, linya, down to langjun and guards—all were divided into Northern and Southern, yet in substance all governed Northern Face affairs; those who speak of Liao offices need not be confused.

units.zh: 凡遼朝官，北樞密視兵部，南樞密視吏部，北、南二王視戶部，夷離畢視刑部，宣徽視工部，敵烈麻都視禮部，北、南府宰相總之。
units.en: Broadly, Northern Privy Council stood for War, Southern Privy for Personnel, the two Great Kings for Revenue, yilibi for Justice, xuanhui for Works, dilie mada for Rites, with Northern and Southern Chancellors above them.
units.literal: In general Liao offices: the Northern Privy Council corresponded to the Ministry of War, the Southern Privy Council to the Ministry of Personnel, the Northern and Southern Great Kings to the Ministry of Revenue, yilibi to the Ministry of Justice, xuanhui to the Ministry of Works, dilie mada to the Ministry of Rites, and the Northern and Southern Chancellors presided over all.

units.zh: 惕隱治宗族，林牙修文告，於越坐而論議，以象公師，朝廷之上。
units.en: Tithen oversaw the imperial clan, linya drafted state papers, and yuyue deliberated from his seat as a notional chief mentor at court.
units.literal: Tithen governed the clans; linya revised documents and proclamations; yuyue sat to discuss policy, representing the duke and tutor at court.

units.zh: 事簡職專，此遼所以興也。
units.en: Simple tasks and focused posts were how Liao prospered.
units.literal: Affairs simple and duties focused—this is why Liao rose.

units.zh: 契丹北樞密院。
units.en: The Khitan Northern Privy Council.
units.literal: Khitan Northern Privy Council.

units.zh: 掌兵機、武銓、群牧之政，凡契丹軍馬皆屬焉。
units.en: It held military planning, military appointments, and herd administration; all Khitan forces and herds fell under it.
units.literal: It governed military affairs, military appointments, and herd administration; all Khitan troops and horses belonged to it.

units.zh: 以其牙帳居大內帳殿之北，故名北院。
units.en: Its yurt headquarters lay north of the inner account hall, hence the Northern Court.
units.literal: Because its headquarters tent stood north of the great inner account hall, it was called the Northern Court.

units.zh: 元好問所謂「北衙不理民」是也。
units.en: As Yuan Haowen said, "the Northern Office does not govern civilians."
units.literal: This is what Yuan Haowen called "the Northern Office does not govern the people."

units.en: The Khitan Southern Privy Council.
units.literal: Khitan Southern Privy Council.

units.zh: 掌文銓、部族、丁賦之政，凡契丹人民皆屬焉。
units.en: It handled civil appointments, tribal registers, and household levies; all Khitan subjects came under it.
units.literal: It governed civil appointments, tribes, and household levies; all Khitan people belonged to it.

units.zh: 以其牙帳居大內之南，故名南院。
units.en: Its yurt headquarters lay south of the inner palace, hence the Southern Court.
units.literal: Because its headquarters tent stood south of the great inner palace, it was called the Southern Court.

units.zh: 元好問所謂「南衙不主兵」是也。
units.en: As Yuan Haowen said, "the Southern Office does not command armies."
units.literal: This is what Yuan Haowen called "the Southern Office does not command troops."

units.en: Originally Dieci yilijin; Taizu split north and south; in Taizong Huitong year 1 the title became Great King.
units.literal: Originally titled yilijin of the Dieci tribe; Taizu divided the Northern and Southern Courts; in Taizong's Huitong year 1 yilijin was changed to Great King.

units.en: Great Yuyue Office
units.literal: Great Yuyue Office.

units.zh: 無職掌，班百僚之上，非有大功德者不授，遼國尊官，猶南面之有三公。
units.en: Without portfolio, it ranked above all officials and was granted only for exceptional merit—Liao's highest honor, comparable to the Three Dukes in the Chinese system.
units.literal: It had no duties; its rank stood above the hundred officials; only those of great merit and virtue received it; it was a honored office of the Liao state, like the Three Dukes on the Southern Face.

units.zh: 太祖以遙輦氏於越受禪。
units.en: Taizu, as yuyue of the Yaolian clan, received the abdication.
units.literal: Taizu, as the Yaolian clan's yuyue, received the abdication.

units.zh: 終遼之世，以於越得重名者三人：耶律曷魯、屋質、仁先，謂之三於越。
units.en: Only three men in Liao history bore the yuyue title with real weight—Yelü Helu, Wuzhi, and Renxian—the Three Yuyue.
units.literal: Through the Liao dynasty only three men gained the yuyue name for weight: Yelü Helu, Wuzhi, and Renxian—called the Three Yuyue.

units.literal: Great yuyue

units.en: Taizu founded it to oversee clan discipline and education.
units.literal: Taizu established it to govern the imperial clan's moral instruction.

units.zh: 興宗重熙二十一年，耶律義先拜惕隱，戒族人曰：「國家三父房最為貴族，凡天下風化之所自出，不孝不義，雖小不可為。」
units.en: In Xingzong Chongxi year 21 Yelü Yixian became tithen and warned the clan: "The Three Fathers' lines are the highest nobility and the source of public morals—no unfilial or unjust act, however slight, is permissible."
units.literal: In Xingzong Chongxi year 21 Yelü Yixian was appointed tithen and admonished the clansmen: "The state's Three Fathers' accounts are the noblest kin; all customs under Heaven flow from them—unfilial and unrighteous acts, however small, must not be done."

units.zh: 其妻晉國長公主之女，每見中表，必具禮服。
units.en: His wife was the Jin State Senior Princess's daughter; she always wore full court dress when receiving kin.
units.literal: His wife was daughter of the Jin State Senior Princess; whenever she met cousins she always wore full ceremonial dress.

units.zh: 義先以身率先，國族化之。
units.en: Yixian led by example and the imperial kin followed.
units.literal: Yixian took the lead in person and the state clans were transformed by it.

units.zh: 遼國設官之實，於此可見。
units.en: Here one sees what Liao offices were really for.
units.literal: The substance of how Liao established offices can be seen here.

units.zh: 太祖有國，首設此官，其後百官擇人，必先宗姓。
units.en: Taizu created this post at the founding; later, when filling the bureaucracy, clan members were chosen first.
units.literal: When Taizu founded the state he first set up this office; afterward in selecting officials for the hundred offices the imperial surname always came first.

units.en: The Three Sovereigns were sages; even in the plainest age, night watches at the gates were stricter than indulging intruders.
units.literal: The Three Sovereigns were sages; even in an age of plain simplicity, beating clappers at the double gates was still stricter than receiving violent guests.

units.en: Before cities and palaces, Liao ancestors camped in carts and fortified felt enclosures—so account-guard posts had to be rigorous.
units.literal: Liao's forebears had no walled cities, moats, or solid palaces; felt carts were camps and hard stockades were palaces—Imperial Account offices had to be strict.

units.zh: 出於貴戚為侍衛，著帳為近侍，北南部族為護衛，武臣為宿衛，親軍為禁衛，百官番宿為宿直。
units.en: Kin of rank became attendants, account registrants close attendants, north and south tribes guards, warriors night guards, household troops forbidden guards, and civil officials rotated as night watch.
units.literal: Noble kin served as attendants; those registered to the account were close attendants; Northern and Southern tribes were guards; military men were night guards; personal troops were forbidden guards; officials of the hundred offices took turns as night duty.

units.zh: 奉宸以司供禦，三班以肅會朝，硬寨以嚴晨夜。
units.en: Fengchen supplied the ruler, the Three Shifts kept assembly order, and hard stockades secured day and night.

units.en: Perhaps this explains why Liao suffered so many coups from within.
